content.title: Conditionals and hypothetical language: rewrite the sentence
content.instructions: Rewrite each sentence following the cue so that the meaning stays the same. Write the complete new sentence. Think about whether the situation is a general truth, a real future possibility, an imaginary present, or an imaginary past.

items.prompt: Many people don't recycle because there are too few recycling points in residential areas. Rewrite starting 'If there …'
accepted_answers: If there were more recycling points in residential areas, more people would recycle.
If there were more recycling points in residential areas, many more people would recycle.
If there weren't so few recycling points in residential areas, more people would recycle.
items.model_answer: If there were more recycling points in residential areas, more people would recycle.
items.explanation: An imaginary present situation takes the second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb. Notice that the negative real situation (too few) becomes a positive hypothetical one (more).

items.prompt: The government didn't invest in flood defences, so the town was badly damaged in 2019. Rewrite starting 'If the government …'
accepted_answers: If the government had invested in flood defences, the town would not have been badly damaged in 2019.
If the government had invested in flood defences, the town wouldn't have been badly damaged in 2019.
If the government had invested in flood defences, the town would not have been so badly damaged in 2019.
items.model_answer: If the government had invested in flood defences, the town would not have been so badly damaged in 2019.
items.explanation: An imaginary past situation takes the third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle. Here the main clause is also passive (would not have been damaged).

items.prompt: I didn't study economics at university, so I don't really understand these statistics now. Rewrite starting 'If I had …'
accepted_answers: If I had studied economics at university, I would understand these statistics now.
If I had studied economics at university, I would really understand these statistics now.
If I had studied economics at university, I would understand these statistics better now.
items.model_answer: If I had studied economics at university, I would understand these statistics now.
items.explanation: A mixed conditional links an imaginary past cause (If + past perfect) to an imaginary present result (would + base verb). The word 'now' signals that the result is in the present, so 'would have understood' is wrong here.

items.prompt: Prices rise whenever demand exceeds supply. Rewrite starting 'If …'
accepted_answers: If demand exceeds supply, prices rise.
If demand exceeds supply, prices go up.
If demand is greater than supply, prices rise.
items.model_answer: If demand exceeds supply, prices rise.
items.explanation: General truths and scientific or economic facts take the zero conditional: If + present simple, present simple. 'If' here means 'whenever'.

items.prompt: Governments must act now, or global temperatures will rise by more than 2°C. Rewrite starting 'Unless …'
accepted_answers: Unless governments act now, global temperatures will rise by more than 2°C.
Unless governments take action now, global temperatures will rise by more than 2°C.
items.model_answer: Unless governments act now, global temperatures will rise by more than 2°C.
items.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if … not' and is used in the first conditional for a real future possibility: Unless + present simple, will + base verb. Do not add 'will' or a negative in the 'unless' clause.

items.prompt: I regret that I didn't learn a second language when I was a child. Rewrite starting 'I wish …'
accepted_answers: I wish I had learnt a second language when I was a child.
I wish I had learned a second language when I was a child.
I wish that I had learnt a second language when I was a child.
items.model_answer: I wish I had learnt a second language when I was a child.
items.explanation: To express regret about the past, use 'wish + past perfect'. For a wish about the present, use 'wish + past simple' (I wish I spoke Spanish). This is valuable in Speaking Part 3 when discussing education.

items.prompt: It's a pity that public transport in my city is so unreliable. Rewrite starting 'If only …'
accepted_answers: If only public transport in my city were more reliable.
If only public transport in my city was more reliable.
If only public transport in my city weren't so unreliable.
items.model_answer: If only public transport in my city were more reliable.
items.explanation: 'If only' is a stronger form of 'I wish'. For a present situation it takes the past simple; 'were' is preferred in formal English for all persons, although 'was' is also accepted.

items.prompt: Governments should start taxing private jets; they have waited far too long. Rewrite starting 'It's high time …'
accepted_answers: It's high time governments started taxing private jets.
It's high time governments taxed private jets.
It's high time that governments started taxing private jets.
items.model_answer: It's high time governments started taxing private jets.
items.explanation: 'It's (high) time + subject + past simple' says that something should already have happened. The past tense has present meaning here, as in other hypothetical structures.

items.prompt: Imagine that all cars were banned from city centres. What would happen to local shops? Rewrite as ONE question starting 'Supposing …'
accepted_answers: Supposing all cars were banned from city centres, what would happen to local shops?
Supposing that all cars were banned from city centres, what would happen to local shops?
items.model_answer: Supposing all cars were banned from city centres, what would happen to local shops?
items.explanation: 'Supposing' (like 'imagine' and 'what if') introduces a hypothetical situation and is followed by the same tenses as a second conditional: past simple in the condition, 'would' in the result.

items.prompt: Without international aid, the country would not have recovered so quickly after the earthquake. Rewrite starting 'If it …'
accepted_answers: If it had not been for international aid, the country would not have recovered so quickly after the earthquake.
If it hadn't been for international aid, the country would not have recovered so quickly after the earthquake.
If it hadn't been for international aid, the country wouldn't have recovered so quickly after the earthquake.
items.model_answer: If it had not been for international aid, the country would not have recovered so quickly after the earthquake.
items.explanation: 'If it had not been for + noun' is a fixed third-conditional expression meaning 'without' in the past. For the present, use 'If it were not for + noun'.
